story:
The svartalfar of Svarhamr say that a drakulv is born without a name, as a wolf cub is, and is given one by the hollow when it is given work. The name comes with the work and belongs to it. When a drakulv who keeps one of the camps dies, the beam-cutters of Svarhamr carve the name, and the holding has the name again by the next moon, because another has taken the work.

Bjornvarg is the exception everyone at Svarhamr knows. The name means bear-wolf, and it was given to the largest of the drakulv who stand on the southern approach to her hollow, where the ground falls away and the ruins give out. The svartalfar say that the drakulv who first held it had a brother of the same litter, of the same size, who would not stand behind him; and that the dragon, asked to choose, did not choose. She gave the name twice. One Bjornvarg stands among the protectors at the southern edge, where the wind comes up off the white country beyond; the other stands further in, among the executioners. They do not speak. The beam has the name cut on it many times and the beam-cutters no longer try to say which brother each mark belongs to.

Of all the named drakulv, the bear-wolves are the only ones who have never been heard to call. Other captains of the court howl when they are struck and their camps come running; the Bjornvargs fight in silence with whatever stands at their shoulder, as if calling for help were something only a lesser name would do. Brisa the beam-cutter says it is pride. The drovers of Gotar, who have heard the story from the svartalfar, say it is simpler than that: there is nothing in Malmohus that a bear-wolf would want to share a kill with.

Hrolleif, who stands near the southern Bjornvarg, is the other half of that saying. Where the bear-wolf is silent, Hrolleif is never quiet, and the svartalfar say the two were set together for exactly that reason.
legend: There are two Bjornvargs up at once in the far south of Malmohus, both level 56 and huge: one with a couple of drakulv protectors near the southern edge, the other a bit further north among drakulv executioners. Neither has any special ability, neither is CC-immune, and unlike most named drakulv they have no faction, so they never bring friends from the camps. The catch is the drakulv standing right next to them: protectors and executioners are 54-67 and will see the fight, so clear or mez them first. Hrolleif stands about a thousand units from the southern Bjornvarg and he DOES bring friends, so don't drag the fight toward him. A good group at 50 handles one Bjornvarg at a time.

aggro: Bear-wolf does not call. Bear-wolf does not need to.
You came up the southern way. Nobody comes up the southern way.
Stand still. I am bigger than you.

phases.text: Still no help. Still none wanted.

death: Cut it... on the beam... the right brother...
The other one... keeps the name...

lairEntry: The ruins give out. A great drakulv stands silent.
Wind off the white country. The bear-wolf waits.

phases.text: Bjornvarg does not howl. He never has.

loremasterTopic.text: The bear-wolf: a name of the [drakulv] given twice, to two brothers the dragon would not choose between. They never call for help, which is why they stand beside [Hrolleif]. See [the names].

bookPage: From the readings of Brisa the beam-cutter of Svarhamr: the hardest marks on the beam are the bear-wolves. A name on our beam is a cut and a dot for each time it is taken again, and for every other drakulv I can read the dots like a family. Bjornvarg I cannot. There are two dots for most winters. My teacher said that once, early, both bear-wolves died in a single season and both names were taken again by the next moon, by two more brothers of one litter, and she cut it, and said she would not cut it with a steady hand again. She was right. Mine shakes too.
